messages.subject: Re: Using the library to get index values for non-square plant distributions
parts:
Hey there,

Thanks for asking us... It will be great to see an example like a print from your original image (good resolution is not necessarily).

You can draw different shape files using the function fieldPolygon(). You can draw your polygons (any shape necessary) selecting regions where you want to extract vegetation indices. Here is some more information: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P15 

You also can draw your shapefile using QGIS and import it to R to extract information (item 4 in this link https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P20).

Hope it helps...!

All the best,
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: Using the library to get index values for non-square plant distributions
parts:
Thank you for sharing the images. I might be mistaken, but it looks like you can use the fieldRotate function to reorient the plots into a rectangle: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#3-rotating-the-image

For removing soil where the background is green, I suggest trying a range of indices to observe which best differentiates between soil and the tree canopy. To test many indices at once you can use the fieldIndex function:

indices <- fieldIndex(imgstack, Red=1, Green=2, Blue=3, index=c("BI", "BIM", "SCI", "GLI", "HI", "NGRDI", "SI", "VARI", "HUE", "BGI"))

If you have multispectral data with RedEdge and/or Near-Infrared (NIR) channels, you can also include the additional indices: PSRI, NDVI, GNDVI, RVI, NDRE, TVI, CVI, CIG, CIRE, DVI, EVI

Best,
Noah
